one_line: Eastern Ganga king Anangabhima Deva III and his general Vishnu, defending Odisha’s independence against Bengal’s pressure in early 13th‑century eastern India.

appearance.age_look: Anangabhima appears in his early 40s with a commanding, athletic build; Vishnu appears in his late 30s, slightly leaner but muscular and battle-hardened.
appearance.face: Both have medium-brown complexions; Anangabhima’s face is oval with a strong jaw, straight nose, neatly trimmed mustache and calm, resolute eyes; Vishnu’s is sharper with a faint jawline stubble, a small scar under his left eye, and a focused, intense gaze; default expression for both is serious, dignified determination.
appearance.hair: Anangabhima’s thick black hair is tied in a high, smooth topknot at the back of the crown, wrapped with a narrow golden band; Vishnu’s slightly wavy black hair is pulled into a lower warrior’s knot at the back of the head, held by a simple dark bronze ring, with a few short loose strands near the temples; neither wears a helmet, but Anangabhima has a slim cloth headband under the gold band in muted red.
appearance.costume: Anangabhima wears a long, ankle-length silk angavastra-style robe in deep saffron-orange wrapped over a fitted off‑white cotton tunic, with a forest‑green border featuring simple repeated geometric motifs, and a broad dark-red sash tied firmly at the waist; over this he has a short, sleeveless quilted protective vest in muted bronze-brown leather with subtle stitched panels, plus simple bronze armlets and a narrow beaded necklace evoking Jagannath devotion; his lower garment is a cream cotton dhoti, pleated to the front and secured by the sash, and he has brown leather sandals. Vishnu wears a darker, more utilitarian outfit: a knee-length indigo cotton tunic belted with a sturdy dark-brown leather war‑belt, over a tightly wrapped pale beige cotton dhoti with practical, narrowed folds for movement; he has a thicker, quilted cotton gambeson in dull olive‑green under a set of small overlapping bronze lamellar plates on the chest and shoulders (no fantastical shapes, just simple rectangular plates), plus forearm guards in dark leather and a pragmatic narrow maroon scarf looped once around his neck; his sandals are reinforced dark-brown leather with simple straps.
appearance.signature: Anangabhima carries a ceremonial yet functional straight steel sword with a slightly broad leaf-shaped blade, a simple cross-guard and an ornate bronze hilt shaped like a stylized wheel, sheathed in a dark-brown leather scabbard with green and saffron bindings; Vishnu carries a battle-worn steel spear about his own height, with a leaf-shaped blade, a plain wooden shaft wrapped in dark-brown leather at the grip and a small saffron cloth knot tied just below the spearhead.

ref_desc: Anangabhima Deva III and General Vishnu appear as two medium-brown, strong-built men with topknot hairstyles, saffron and indigo dhoti-based war garb, modest bronze armour, a Jagannath-themed sword and a leather-wrapped spear, in a palette of saffron, green, indigo, bronze, and dark brown.
sheet_prompt: Draw two full-body anime-style male figures from early 13th-century eastern India standing side by side: Anangabhima Deva III and his general Vishnu. Anangabhima is slightly older and broader, medium-brown complexion, oval face with strong jaw, calm serious eyes and a neatly trimmed mustache. His thick black hair is tied in a high smooth topknot, wrapped with a narrow golden band over a muted red cloth headband. He wears a long ankle-length saffron-orange silk angavastra-style robe over a fitted off-white cotton tunic, the robe edged with a forest-green border of simple repeated geometric motifs, and a broad dark-red sash tightly cinched at his waist. Beneath, a cream cotton dhoti is pleated to the front and wrapped traditionally, and his sandals are brown leather. Over his torso he has a short sleeveless quilted bronze-brown leather vest for protection, with subtle stitched panels, plus simple bronze armlets and a narrow beaded necklace hinting at Jagannath devotion. In his hand or at his side is his signature straight steel sword: a slightly broad leaf-shaped blade with a plain cross-guard and an ornate bronze hilt shaped like a stylized wheel, sheathed in a dark-brown leather scabbard bound with green and saffron. Beside him stands Vishnu, slightly younger, lean but muscular, medium-brown complexion, sharper face with a faint stubble, a small scar under his left eye and a focused, intense gaze. His slightly wavy black hair is pulled into a lower warrior’s knot at the back of his head, held by a simple dark bronze ring with a few short loose strands near the temples. He wears an indigo knee-length cotton tunic belted with a sturdy dark-brown leather war-belt over a tightly wrapped pale beige cotton dhoti with narrowed folds for mobility, reinforced dark-brown leather sandals, and a dull olive-green quilted gambeson under small overlapping bronze lamellar plates on chest and shoulders, plus dark leather forearm guards and a narrow maroon scarf looped once around his neck. His signature weapon is a battle-worn steel spear about his own height, with a leaf-shaped blade, a plain wooden shaft wrapped in dark-brown leather at the grip and a small saffron cloth knot tied just below the spearhead. Use a cohesive palette of saffron orange, forest green, indigo blue, bronze and dark brown, and show them in dignified, era-accurate, modest heroic poses ready to defend Odisha’s independence in a realistic historical anime style.
